Ksiaz Wielki Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Książ Wielki, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Książ Wielki in the 18th century, reaching 852 (49.7%) by 1921, mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942; the remaining 11 Jews left by 1945 for their own safety. This cemetery, established around 1847 with a funeral house and gravedigger's residence added by 1859, was fenced by the early 20th century and valued at 6,000 zlotys (including the funeral house) by 1935. Germans carried out executions here during WWII; Poland formally closed the cemetery on November 4, 1964, with documentation noting its last burial in 1943. By the 1980s, the grounds were used as pasture, with a pile of loose matzevot found on site. The Nissenbaum Family Foundation fenced the cemetery between 1987-1991.
